hero.description: A bicycle loop is the human-speed version of Vang Vieng: cross the Nam Song, leave the town traffic behind and let rice fields, villages and limestone walls become the main itinerary.
steps: Check brakes and tyres before leaving
Carry water and a basic repair option
Build the loop around one or two stops, not every attraction
hero.rhythmNote: The route quality changes with rain and road works. A shorter loop ridden comfortably is better than forcing a fixed distance through mud, heat or fading daylight.

chapters.label: THE SPEED
chapters.title: Fast enough to explore, slow enough to notice the valley
chapters.body: Vang Vieng's west bank is easy to flatten into a list of lagoons and viewpoints when you move by motorbike. On a bicycle, the roads, fields and distances become the experience. That slower scale is the reason to ride.

chapters.label: THE LOOP
chapters.title: One strong stop is enough
chapters.body: Build the ride around a single swim, cave or easy viewpoint and leave space between them. Cycling becomes much less enjoyable when every turn is timed against a checklist of entrances.

note.label: ATLAS NOTE
note.text: The best cycling day in Vang Vieng is not the one with the most attractions. It is the one where the road still feels like part of the trip.

chapters.label: THE BIKE
chapters.title: A two-minute check can save the half day
chapters.body: Before leaving the rental shop, test both brakes, tyre pressure, gears if fitted and saddle height. Ask what happens if you get a puncture away from town and photograph any existing damage.

beforeYouLeave.title: Use the weather to size the loop
beforeYouLeave.body: Start smaller in heat or after heavy rain. You can always add distance once the surface and your energy are clear; cutting an ambitious route late in the day is harder.

note.label: ROUTE RULE
note.text: Early start · one anchor stop · flexible distance.

items.label: Time
items.detail: Enough for a relaxed loop with one or two meaningful stops.

items.label: Bike check
items.detail: Test the bicycle before leaving the rental shop.

items.label: Roads
items.detail: Rain can turn local dirt roads slower and rougher; adapt the loop instead of forcing it.

items.label: Carry
items.detail: Shade is inconsistent and the heat can make modest distances feel much longer.

faq.question: Is Vang Vieng good for cycling?
faq.answer: Yes if you want to explore the west-bank countryside at a slower pace. The karst roads and fields are as important as the individual stops.

faq.question: How long should I rent a bike?
faq.answer: A half day is a good starting point. Take a full day only if you want several stops and are comfortable with the road and heat.

faq.question: What should I check on the rental bike?
faq.answer: Test both brakes, tyre pressure, gears if present and saddle height, and ask what support exists for a puncture.

faq.question: What should I combine with the ride?
faq.answer: Choose one lagoon, cave or compact viewpoint rather than trying to collect every attraction on the west bank.

faq.question: Bicycle or motorbike for the west bank?
faq.answer: Choose a bicycle when you want the road and countryside to be the experience. Choose a motorbike when covering distance between several attractions matters more.
